title: Split setup_searxng.sh under the 250-line cap
objective: Bring linux_configuration/scripts/single_use/features/setup_searxng.sh (912 lines) under the cap, and establish the verification a split must pass when the moved code generates service configuration.
acceptance_criteria: The entry script and all six new libs are at most 250 lines.
The pre-commit shellcheck hook passes on every touched file, with no new suppression and no disable directive.
No lib sources a sibling: the entry script sources all six directly.
The stubbed run reports every moved function as defined.

The content the script generates is byte-identical: comparing the non-comment lines of the original write_stack against the three functions it became must produce the same hash. A split that quietly altered a compose file or settings.yml would pass every other check.
The comment explaining why settings.yml is mode 640 rather than 600 travels with the code it explains.
out_of_scope: Executing the setup, starting containers or reloading Caddy.
The other very large scripts (setup_nextcloud_raspberry.sh, check_and_enable_services.sh and the rest), which are separate commits.
verifier: meta/scripts/verify_shell_split.sh, plus an md5 comparison of the sorted non-comment lines of the original write_stack against its three successor functions, plus pre-commit run --files and check_file_length.sh.
